container.noneYet: No containers on this character yet. Use “Annotate carrying gear” to flag packs and sacks this character already carries, or the box control beside an item to make anything a container.
container.emptyHint: empty — drag gear here to stow it
container.empty: Empty the container (contents stay on the character)
container.setDown: Set this container and everything in it down where you stand
container.unmake: Stop treating this as a container
container.wornHint: Worn or wielded — stowing it will unequip it first.
container.correction: RAW corrections applied: {stone} st {direction} (adventurer's harness / bowquiver).
container.noActor: Select a token or assign a character first.
container.foreignItem: Only gear already on this character can be stowed.

storeFailed.selfContained: An item cannot be put inside itself.
storeFailed.notStowable: {item} cannot be stowed in a container.
storeFailed.cycle: {container} is already inside {item} — that would nest them in a loop.

notify.autoUnequipped: Auto-unequipped to keep a legal loadout: {items}.
notify.namedAdvanced: {item} reveals more of its power to {name}.
notify.namedRevealed: {item} answers to its true name — its full powers awaken.

ammo.firedSilver: {ammo} — silver, counts as extraordinary damage: {left} left.
ammo.threwSingle: {item} thrown — recover it to reclaim its weight.

grip.cycle: Grip: {grip} — click to cycle one-handed / two-handed / auto
grip.blocked: Wants a two-handed grip but both hands are not free — free a hand or drop the shield

light.light: Light this source (uses a free hand)

action.readied: Readied a torch from the stack.
action.readyHint: Ready a torch — pull one from the stack to wield, light, or throw.
action.noStock: No {item} left in the stack to ready.
action.notReadiable: {item} is not a torch stack; nothing to ready.
action.scavengeHint: Scavenged equipment — roll a condition onto this item and apply its mechanical effects.
action.scavengePrompt: Roll a random condition and stamp it onto this item's own fields (damage / attack / AC / weight). It can be cleared back to pristine at any time.

masterwork.title: Masterwork — {name}
masterwork.prompt: Apply a masterwork quality (RR p. 159). It is written onto the item's own fields and can be cleared back to None at any time.

itemLoss.title: Item loss: {name}
itemLoss.rear: Damaged from the flank or rear (reverses the order)
itemLoss.off: Item loss is off. Turn on "{setting}" in the module settings first.
itemLoss.noActor: Select a token or assign a character first.
itemLoss.notLowEnough: No equipment is at risk at that hit point total (JJ p. 398).
itemLoss.nothing: Nothing is vulnerable to that damage type.
itemLoss.skipped: {n} item(s) were not vulnerable to this damage type and were skipped.
itemLoss.riskTip: Counted from the hit points after the attack, against the imported threshold ({threshold} hp) and step ({step} hp). {cite}
itemLoss.destroyTip: {weight} st, within the {light} st a light item runs to. {cite}
itemLoss.damageTip: {weight} st, at or over the {heavy} st a heavy item starts at. {cite}
itemLoss.acTip: {stones} full stone of damage at {per} AC per stone. {cite}
itemLoss.marredTip: {weight} st, within the {light} st a light item runs to, but only {left} st of the loss was left when it was reached. {cite}
itemLoss.unplacedTip: {weight} st, between {light} st and {heavy} st. The import holds no case for that weight, so it is yours to rule. {cite}
itemLoss.factTip: {weight} st. Light up to {light} st, heavy from {heavy} st. {cite}
itemLoss.restoreTip: Item loss has taken {n} AC from this armor. Restoring gives it back and changes nothing else on the item.
itemLoss.restoreBody: Give {name} back the {n} AC item loss took from it?

printed.editedByHand: Edited by hand on {name}; the import read it from {cite}.

strap.cycle: Carry position — click to cycle in hand / on the back / on the front. A strapped shield costs no hand.

variant.cycle: Shield variant — click to choose buckler, kite, phalanx, and so on.
variant.title: Shield variant — {name}
variant.prompt: Choose which shield this is. Its AC benefit, encumbrance, and carry options follow from the variant.

props.weaponTypeNone: Unidentified: nothing names which weapon this is. Proficiency category, size and damage type fall back to their defaults, so a character trained on this weapon can still be told it is non-proficient. Pick the type above.
props.figureDeclared: {figure}: set on this item, which outranks the weapon table.
props.figureFromRow: {figure}: read from the {weapon} row of the weapon table ({cite}).
props.figureFromRowNoPage: {figure}: read from the {weapon} row of the weapon table.
props.gripsHint: Which hands this may be held in — both lit is either. Lit dashed while the size table answers; a click declares it.
props.gripsAuto: Auto: {grips}, from the weapon's size (RR p. 127).
props.qualitiesHint: The weapon's uses and the system's special weapon properties, as its own sheet records them. The attack throw reads these.
props.otherTagsHint: Free text, for what no quality above names.
props.conditionCite: Rows read from your own book: {cite}.
props.conditionImported: Rows read from your own book.
props.conditionJudge: Rows set by hand in the Ruledata Browser.
props.materialNote: Destroyed by: {types} (item loss). No standing modifier.
props.materialNoneNote: No damage type destroys this material (item loss).
props.masterworkReachNote: Masterwork edits this weapon's numbers only; what it can harm is unchanged (RR p. 159).
props.silverNote: This item counts as silvered (RR p. 159).
props.silverNoneNote: This item does not count as silvered (RR p. 159).
props.slotHint: Every place this may sit. Lit dashed while inferred from the name and type; a click declares it. None lit is carried — worn nowhere.
props.handsLocked: A weapon is held: its hands are its own and are not offered.
props.slotInferred: Auto: {slots}, from the item's name and type.
props.slotCapacity: {slot} holds {n} magic item(s) and one equippable item (Treasure Tome).
props.slotCapacityRead: {slot} holds {n} magic item(s) and one equippable item ({source}).
props.autoHint: Return the answer to inference — the item's name, its type and its table row.

helm.cycle: Helmet type — click to make it a heavy (enclosing) helm.
helm.heavyHint: Enclosing helmet: its modifiers apply to the wearer (RR p. 140); core applies the Mortal Wounds one to an item whose name holds "heavy" and "helmet". Click to make it light.

spellbook.manageHint: Edit the spells recorded in this book. Its value follows from their levels (RR p. 391).
spellbook.title: Spell book — {name}
spellbook.prompt: One spell per line, its level as a trailing number after a comma. The pages used follow from the levels (RR p. 145).

tip.used: Pages used: the levels of the spells recorded in this book, summed (RR p. 145).

what.blank: Price of a blank spell book
what.scribing: Value of one scribed spell level

disguise.hint: GM: give this item an apparent (mundane) identity — players see the disguise, not the truth.
disguise.activeHint: Disguised (true: {name}). Click to edit or reveal.
disguise.title: Apparent identity — {name}
disguise.prompt: What players should see. The true stats stay hidden until you Reveal; the real weight is unchanged so it can still be carried. Sheet-level only — not encrypted.
disguise.off: Not disguised — players see this item as it really is.

named.badge: Named item — {n}/{max} powers unlocked. Click to open.
named.badgeNone: Not a named item. Click to name it (GM).
named.guessBlank: Type the name to speak first.
named.noSpeaker: No character to speak the name (open it from an actor, or assign your character).
named.noGuess: {name} has a guess recorded for this level already (JJ p. 399).
named.correct: The name is TRUE — {item} awakens to its full power.
named.wrong: That is not the name. A guess is recorded for {name} at this level (JJ p. 399).
named.gmHint: Ladder categories: hit, damage, ac, encumbrance, power. The Judge sets the order.
named.noLadder: No unlock ladder set — the Judge chooses the order (fields below): hit, damage, ac, encumbrance, power.
named.overlayOff: Level-up advancement is OFF — enable “Overlay: named magic items (JJ)” in settings to automate it.
named.renamed: The item is now called “{item}” — one of its powers stirs.

variations.removeHint: Take this variation off. The item's numbers go back to what they were without it.
variations.revealHint: Show this to the players. This is what identifying an item is.
variations.concealHint: Hide this from the players. They see the item without it, priced without it.
variations.badBaseType: An item of this kind cannot be {type}.

refuse.wrongBaseType: {key} does not go on an item of this kind.
refuse.familyClash: This already has {key}, and an item has only one of those.
refuse.supersedes: This would supersede {key}, which it already has.
refuse.selfContained: A variation cannot be applied to itself.
refuse.legacyClash: This item already records {key} in its own field above. Clear that first.

hint.key: Namespaced, like masterwork.weaponToHit. Everything before the first dot is the group: an item carries one variation from each group.
hint.appliesTo: Base types, comma separated. Leave blank for anything.
hint.supersedes: Keys this replaces, comma separated. A trailing .* matches a whole group. Leave blank unless a page says otherwise.
hint.weight6: Six to the stone. Negative makes the item lighter.
hint.costOrder: Applied in this order: the listed price is scaled, the surcharge is added, then the whole is scaled.
hint.hidden: The players see the item without this, and priced without it. What it does still applies.
hint.read: Off means it can be seen but not understood.
hint.language: The tongue it is written in, if reading it needs one.

band.quantity: How many are in the stack.
band.weightHint: Weight in sixths of a stone. Six to the stone. Where the item states a bundle size, this is the weight of one bundle.
band.perStoneHint: How many of these weigh one stone. Blank weighs them as the system weighs coin.
band.valueHint: Listed price, in gold pieces. Plating, masterwork, variations and condition build on it in Details; where they change it, the worth reads beside the field.
band.openScene: Open the scene this chart draws.
band.conditionHint: Visible to everyone — damage cannot be disguised.
band.maskedHint: Players see the disguise. You see the true item.

condition.materialHint: Decides which damage types can destroy it (item loss).

value.coin: What the stack is worth — its count at the value of one.
value.apparent: Apparent worth — what it passes for until identified.
value.trueValue: True value — players see the disguise's.
value.unknown: Marked unappraised in Details — nobody has put a price on it.

hint.priced: Apparent worth until identified, then the full price.
hint.unknown: Nobody has appraised it; the badge reads Unknown.
hint.na: Not a saleable item — the badge reads a dash.

rail.emptyRoll: Empty roll slot — pin a roll on the Rolls tab.
rail.moreRolls: More rolls than the art carries — open the Rolls tab.
rail.equipHint: Worn or wielded. Click to toggle.
rail.readyHint: A torch stack is carried, not held — click to ready one torch and draw it.
rail.splitHint: A stack cannot be equipped — click to split one out and equip it.
rail.restackHint: One split from its stack and equipped — click to return it.
rail.favoriteHint: Pinned to the character sheet's favourites.
rail.capacityHint: How full it is — open Contents.
rail.lockHint: Locked — open Durability for the lock.

aura.title: Aura
aura.hint: Detectable before identification — a disguise does not mask it.

curse.told: The players have been told this item is cursed (JJ ch. 4, Identifying Magic Items).
curse.secret: Judge's mark: this item is cursed and the players have not been told (JJ ch. 4, Identifying Magic Items).

field.perHint: How many units one stated weight covers. Leave at 1 unless the weight is given for a bundle.
field.perStoneHint: How many of these weigh one stone. Blank weighs them as the system weighs coin.

rolls.noneHint: Nothing on this item throws dice.
rolls.noRoller: Nobody to roll: open the item from a character, control a token, or assign your character.

maneuver.byHand: the value set in the Ruledata Browser

chart.frameHint: Drawn from the scene's explored fog of war — dark ground is uncharted.
chart.captureAlt: The explored ground, as last captured.
chart.caption: Fog of war capture
chart.blankHint: Nothing captured yet — redraw it from exploration.
chart.updateHint: Redraw the chart from the ground explored so far.
chart.noScene: The scene this chart drew no longer exists.
chart.noExploration: Nothing has been explored on that scene yet.
chart.updated: Chart redrawn — {pct}% of the scene charted.

lock.title: The Lock
lock.pickHint: A modifier to the Lockpicking throw.
lock.fragileHint: Breaking it open destroys what is inside.

effects.addHint: Adds an effect to this item and opens it. Choose a blank effect or a magic light.
effects.addBlankHint: Blank Effect: an empty effect carried by whoever holds this item, for you to fill in.
effects.addLightHint: Magic Light: an effect that sheds light from whoever wears this item, or carries it outside a container if it cannot be worn, with the reach in feet left for you to type.
effects.mundaneHint: Add an effect, or drop an enchantment onto this item.
effects.unidentifiedHint: Its effects are hidden until it is identified.
effects.nothingGrantedHint: The bearer's class, proficiencies and attributes add nothing to this item.

named.title: The Name
named.trueLine: True name, Judge only · spoken aloud it unlocks every point
named.guessHint: Speak a guess at the true name (JJ p. 399).

contents.dropHint: Drag items here. Locked containers refuse drops from players.
contents.needsActor: Open this container from a character to store gear in it.

know.title: What The Players Know
know.detectedHint: Judge's mark: the players are told this item is magic only once it is detected. Identification marks it detected (JJ ch. 4, Identifying Magic Items).
know.detectedAria: Mark this item's magic as detected by the players
know.cursedHint: Judge's mark: this item is cursed. The players see nothing of it until the curse is known; the mark applies no effect (JJ ch. 4, Identifying Magic Items).
know.curseKnownHint: Judge's mark: the players are told the item is cursed without a full identification. A full identification sets it (JJ ch. 4, Identifying Magic Items).
know.curseKnownAria: Tell the players this item is cursed

hint.none: Held and handled; nothing magical is apparent.
hint.partial: Its nature is known, not its effect or worth.
hint.full: The effect and the worth are known.

note.1: Players see no aura, no effects and only the apparent value.
note.2: Players see the aura and its school; the effects and the value stay hidden.
note.3: Players see everything the sheet holds.

disguise.title: Disguise
disguise.explain: Drop an item here and players see its name, art, description, stats and price in its place — the real effects keep working underneath. The aura is not masked.
disguise.noneHint: Drag an item from a compendium or a sheet onto this panel.

options.title: Options
options.holdsHint: Adds the Contents tab — a chest, a backpack, a quiver, a map case.
options.acceptHint: Nothing selected means the container takes anything that fits; a wrong drop is refused with the message below.
options.refusalHint: What the container says to a wrong drop.
options.magicHint: Judge only — adds the Appearance tab, where identification and the aura live.
options.disguisableHint: Judge only — adds the Appearance tab's disguise drop target.

variations.title: Variations
variations.addHint: Make a variation by hand — published ones are dragged on.

equip.noSlot: This item declares nowhere to be worn.
equip.splitDone: {name} split from the stack and equipped.

itemSheet.locked: Unlock the sheet with the pencil to change it.

ACKS-EQUIPMENT.container.bashConfirm: Break open {name}? The container is destroyed; its contents spill out.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.container.bashConfirmFrag: Break open {name}? It is fragile — the container AND everything inside it are destroyed.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.container.unmake: Stop treating this as a container
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.container.annotateAll: Annotate carrying gear from the RAW capacity table, and coin from the weight its own text states
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.container.lockedHint: Locked. You cannot see what is inside.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.lock.gloved: You cannot pick a lock wearing gloves.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.lock.bashedSpilled: {name} is broken open; {n} item(s) spill out.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.lock.manual.noAbilitiesMo: Roll {ability} yourself — the ability roller is unavailable, so this cannot roll it for you.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.lock.manual.noThrow: {ability} carries no throw on this seat. Connect your book, or roll it yourself.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.lock.manual.unresolved: Rolled — the target could not be resolved here, so the Judge decides whether {name} opens.
ACKS-EQUIPMENT.loadout.title: {name} — Loadout

tableUuid.label: Encounter table
tableUuid.hint: RollTable drawn from (privately) when a wandering-monster encounter triggers while the party token is inside this region. Drag a RollTable here or paste its UUID.

encounterEvery.label: Throw frequency (dungeon turns)
encounterEvery.hint: Make an encounter throw every N dungeon turns inside this zone. A journey does not read this field. 0 = inherit the module setting.

encounterTarget.label: Target value (JJ ch. 2)
encounterTarget.hint: Encounter occurs on this value or higher inside this zone. On a journey this throw replaces the territory throw. 0 = inherit the module setting.

dungeonLevel.label: Dungeon level
dungeonLevel.hint: The dungeon level this zone counts as, compared with the monster level of the table a wandering monster is drawn from (JJ p. 36). 0 = not set: nothing is compared.

journeyCadence.label: Journey cadence
journeyCadence.hint: When a journey throws inside this zone. Blank inherits; Entry throws once as the party crosses into the zone and not per hex inside it; Periods throws only at End Day, the day and night counts below.

dayThrows.label: Day throws (End Day)
dayThrows.hint: Throws made for the day at End Day inside this zone when its cadence is Periods; they replace the day's hunting, searching and resting throws. 0 inherits.

nightThrows.label: Night throws (End Day)
nightThrows.hint: Throws made for the night at End Day inside this zone when its cadence is Periods; they replace the resting night's throw. 0 inherits.

app.title: Exploration Formation
app.addSelectedHint: Add the tokens selected on the canvas to this formation (their tokens are stashed and replaced by the party token)
app.disbandHint: Restore all member tokens around the party token and remove the formation
app.disbandConfirm: Disband {name}? Member tokens will be restored around the party token.
app.casualtyHint: Down. The party cannot move until someone carries them or they are left behind.
app.leftBehindHint: Left where they fell. They still take their share of the experience.
app.addBlankHint: Add an empty slot to the marching grid (swap it into position with the arrows — gaps are kept in combat deployment)
app.shieldHint: Close/open the lantern shutter: sheds no light while closed but keeps burning oil (RR equipment). Mapping needs an open light.
app.frontageHint: How many march abreast. Any width the scene can hold. Groups the list into ranks, lays out the column drawn behind the party token, and shapes combat deployment.

shape.label: On the map
shape.hint: Marching order: the party token is one square at the head and the column is drawn behind it along the ground it walked. Fixed size: the token keeps the size you give it in Token Config, and nothing is drawn. Lights shine from each bearer's place in the order either way.

columnColor.label: Column tint
columnColor.hint: The tint the drawn column's squares wear. Blank takes the party token's disposition colour.

app.stackHint: Stands for several bodies. Open its sheet to record casualties — they come off in one stroke, not one at a time.
app.autoArrangeHint: Staff a full front line (scouts and the best-armoured melee, spears next) and a full back line (Rear Guard, then missile users) first; non-combatants, the mapper and spellcasters hold the middle ranks, centred with blank slots. Tweak afterwards with the arrows.
app.emptyMembers: Drag actors or tokens into this sheet, or right-click a token on the canvas and use its "Add to party" HUD button.
app.trainDeploy: Deploy as a place beside the party
app.trainDeployedHint: Standing as a place: its token is a point of interest on the map.
app.emptyState: No formation yet — right-click a token and use "Add to party", or create a Party Formation actor.
app.speedHint: Party exploration speed, in feet per turn (RR p. 263)
app.magicLightNotSetTip: The effect "{effect}" on {source} names a light but carries no reach. Open the effect and type the feet in its changes.
app.magicLightCastTip: From the light row of {spell}, on {source} ({cite}): {reach}.
app.carryHint: Distance moved that has not yet added up to a full turn
app.advanceTurnHint: Mark off one full dungeon turn.
app.adjustHpHint: Adjust the hit points of this party's members.
app.restTurnHint: Spend a turn resting (RR 271): resets the rest counter and removes Winded
app.encounterNowHint: Make a wandering-monster throw right now (GM-whispered)
app.rationsHint: Consume one ration per member from their inventory
app.undoTurnHint: Roll the clock back one turn (bookkeeping only; world time is not rewound)
app.pauseHint: Pause/resume movement-driven turn tracking (e.g. while repositioning the token)
app.noStashedToken: No stashed token: this member was added without a canvas token and will not be re-placed on disband
app.toggleLightHint: Extinguish or relight (remaining burn time is kept; relighting takes a round via the tinderbox)
app.tableHint: Default RollTable drawn from when a wandering-monster encounter triggers. An ACKS Encounter Zone region under the party token overrides this.
app.spellPickHint: Track a spell known by a member (duration parsed from the spell when it reads like "6 turns")
app.trackSpellHint: Counts down one per dungeon turn; announced when it gutters (1 turn) and expires
app.spellPlusHint: Add one turn (e.g. higher caster level)
app.magicalHint: Magical source: apply each member's Bonus vs Magic and WIS modifier to the roll (uncheck for mundane hazards)
app.saveTooltip: Roll a {save} saving throw for every member against their own sheet's target
app.saveTooltipOwned: Roll a {save} saving throw for each member whose character you own, against their own sheet's target
app.summonStaysBadge: Its control has ended; it stays (RR ch. 5).
app.summonHostileBadge: It turned hostile when its control ended. Only the Judge can dismiss it (RR ch. 5).
app.detachedBadge: Out ahead of the party on their own token
app.detachHint: Detach: step out of the party token onto your own, carrying your own light and seeing with your own eyes. You stay in the formation — turns, rest and encounters keep counting.
app.recallHint: Rejoin the party token, bringing back everything that happened while you were out
app.darkSightHint: How far this character sees with no light at all (lightless vision, or a thief's shadowy senses). Everyone else sees only what a light source reveals.
app.leashed: {name} has gone as far ahead as they can — the party must catch up first.
app.orphanParty: This party actor is not linked to any formation.
app.hurriedBadge: per turn — hurrying at combat pace
app.paceHint: Switches the party between careful exploration and hurried (RR p. 263)
app.downBadge: Down (0 hp or less): carried, not walking — assign Carriers, or leave them behind to march on
app.blindBadge: Cannot see (darkness, no dark senses): moves at {share} of its speed (RR App. B, Blinded)
app.editImageHint: Change the party's image (updates the actor, its prototype token, and the placed token)
app.lightCastSlotsCore: Used {used} of {max}: the slot count on {caster}'s sheet for level {level}

map.noSession: No active map session — exploration is not being drawn onto a map object. Start one with "New Map" (requires a Mapper and viewing the party's scene).
map.notViewing: view the party's scene to archive

state.blockedCombat: A fight is on, so the module pauses mapping.
state.blockedHurried: The party is hurrying, so the module pauses mapping.
state.down: {name}: cannot work (down, dead or left behind).
state.litAssumed: light is assumed (the light requirement is off)

map.newMapHint: Close the current map, wipe the scene's explored fog, and start a fresh map from black — used when the party loses its bearings (fell through a hole, teleported) or starts a new area.
map.newMapConfirm: Start a new map? The scene's explored fog is reset for everyone — the party keeps only what the working map records, and only sees fresh exploration from here on.
map.archiveHint: Copy the current explored area into the working Map item now (also happens automatically each dungeon turn while you view the scene).
map.closeHint: Final archive, then end the session. The Map item stays with its bearer — carry it, sell it, lose it.
map.saveFogHint: Save your current fog view of this scene as a new (accurate) Map item in the sidebar — for authoring maps to sell or hand out.
map.anchorHint: The party has connected its position to territory this map depicts (your judgment): reveal the map's recorded areas on the scene for everyone.
map.anchoredHint: Anchored: this map's record has been revealed on the scene
map.distortedHint: Drawn without Mapping proficiency: the record is subtly wrong and will misalign when anchored
map.needsScene: View the party's scene to manage its map.
map.needsMapper: Assign a Mapper role first — someone has to draw the map.
map.newMapInCombat: A new map cannot be started while the party is in combat.
map.archiveNeedsScene: View the party's scene to archive the map (it will retry each dungeon turn).
map.sessionStarted: {mapper} unrolls a fresh sheet and begins a new map — the old bearings are gone.
map.sessionUnproficient: The mapper lacks Mapping proficiency: this map's record is being distorted (hidden warp). It will misalign when anchored later.
map.sessionClosed: The working map is rolled up and stowed.
map.sessionLostItem: The working Map item is gone (traded, sold, or destroyed) — the map session has ended.
map.wrongScene: That map depicts {scene} — it cannot be anchored here.
map.emptyMap: That map has nothing recorded on it yet.
map.anchored: The party matches "{name}" against their surroundings — its recorded areas are revealed.
map.anchoredDistorted: That map was drawn without Mapping proficiency — the revealed areas are subtly misaligned against the true dungeon. Let them discover the discrepancies.
map.authoredDescription:
A drawn map of {scene}.

Its recorded territory is stored on this item. When the party can match it to their surroundings, the Judge anchors it from the party sheet to reveal the mapped area.
map.authored: Map item "{name}" created in the Items sidebar.
map.itemDescription:
A working map of {scene}, drawn in the field by {mapper}.

The recorded exploration is stored on this item and updates each dungeon turn. Whoever holds it holds the map: trade or loot it freely. When the party can match it to their surroundings, the Judge anchors it from the party sheet to reveal its territory.
map.reasonEmpty: Nothing recorded on this map yet (it archives each dungeon turn while the GM views the scene)
map.reasonScene: This map depicts a different scene than the party's
map.reasonViewing: View the party's scene to anchor (the fog texture only exists for the viewed scene)
map.mergeNeedsScene: View the scene whose fog you want to merge first.
map.mergeWhileAstray: A party on this scene is lost and does not know it yet. Merge fog records once they realise it or the episode ends.
map.mergedCopies: Merged {count} older fog record(s) on this scene into each player's current one; their maps now show everything they explored here.
map.noCopies: No seat has more than one fog record on this scene; nothing to merge.
map.statusLine: Working record updated at turn {turns} of exploring {scene}. The drawn map itself is stored on this item — carry, sell, or loot it; a Judge can Anchor it from the party sheet to reveal its territory.

rolls.listenHint: Every member rolls Listening with their own sheet target; the round is marked off (RR p. 265).
rolls.alreadyListened: The party already listened this turn while moving (RR p. 265).
rolls.searchHastyHint: Members with a Searching skill search hastily; the round is marked off (RR p. 265).
rolls.searchMethodicalHint: Skill users roll with the methodical bonus; anyone else uses their Adventuring target. The turn advances automatically (RR p. 265).
rolls.searchMethodicalNote: Methodical search (RR p. 265). The turn is marked off automatically.
rolls.bashHint: Dungeonbashing adjusted by Strength; the Judge applies a crowbar and size (RR p. 267). The round is marked off.
rolls.bashNote: Stuck doors (RR p. 267). Add a crowbar's bonus by hand.
rolls.nobodyCapable: No member can attempt {check} (no matching skill on any sheet).
rolls.trackingHint: Members with the Tracking proficiency roll; the Judge adjusts the throw for the conditions (RR p. 120). The turn advances automatically.
rolls.trackingNote: Tracking (RR p. 120). The turn is marked off automatically; apply the Judge's modifiers by hand.
rolls.noHastyHurried: The party is hurrying at combat speed — hasty searching is not possible. Slow to a careful pace first.
rolls.trapbreakHastyHint: Takes a round; Trapbreaking skill only (RR p. 267).
rolls.trapbreakMethodicalHint: Takes a turn. A skilled thief rolls with the methodical bonus; anyone else tries through Adventuring (RR p. 267).

membership.bringHint: Your people who are in no party. The table sees who comes and goes.

refused.notYours: {name} is not yours to move in or out of a party.
refused.inParty: {name} is already in {party}. Take them out of it first.
refused.elsewhere: {name} stands on another map from this party.

conveyance.backHint: Clear the word set for the group: each member takes their own choice, or the fastest they have.
conveyance.fastestHint: Each member takes their own choice, or the fastest they have.
conveyance.undoHint: Put everyone back where the last group press found them.
conveyance.pinOut: Their chosen ride cannot take them just now

offerTip.foot: Their own pace, on their own legs.
offerTip.vessel: {name} keeps a voyage's clock, not a march's.

request.hint: Declarations are sent to the Judge's client for execution; a GM must be connected. Search and listen results go to the Judge.
request.noGM: No GM is connected — actions cannot be executed right now.
request.lightHint: Light a torch, lantern, or candle carried by your character (consumes one from inventory)
request.spellHint: Add one of your character's spells to the formation's duration tracker
request.rest: the party rests for a turn
request.restHint: Declare a rest turn (resets the rest clock; recovers winded)
request.askRound: asks the Judge for a Round.
request.askTurn: asks the Judge to spend a turn.
request.searchHere: declares that the party searches here.
request.detachDeclined: That declaration could not be carried out — the party has no token on the canvas to step out from, or the character cannot leave the party right now.
request.refused: The Judge's client did not take that press.
request.paceCareful: slows the party to a careful pace.
request.enterHex: takes the party into the next hex, {hex}.
request.enterHexBlank: takes the party into the next hex.
request.forageDay: works the country for the day.

role.mapperHint: Draws the map. The module has the party map only while a mapper can work and a light reaches where they stand, and reads the scene's measurements exact with the Mapping proficiency and vague without it. Quill and parchment fill both hands, and the module holds Vulnerable on them until the kit is stashed (RR ch. 6, Marching and Mapping).
role.scoutHint: Moves ahead of the front rank in trap-heavy areas (usually a thief). Automatic search reach: {search}; with a pole: {pole} (RR ch. 6, Searching).
role.rearguardHint: Fast-moving or missile-equipped members watching the party's back
role.poleHint: Probes ahead of its bearer for trap activation. Lead: {lead} (RR ch. 6, Traps and Trapbreaking).
role.noncombatantHint: Stays with the party token when combat begins and is not added to the initiative tracker
role.carrierHint: Carries the downed: each carried body's weight is split evenly among the Carriers (RR p. 271), and the load slows their pace and so the party's

mapperVulnerable.effectDescription: Held by the module while this character holds the party's Mapper role (RR ch. 6).

winded.effectDescription: Cannot charge or run until rested (RR p. 271).

chat.scaleGuard: {name} stands on a map whose cell is {miles} mi across; the turn clock bills nothing here. Declare the map's system in the battlemap setup, or begin a journey.
chat.windedStatus: The party is WINDED — no charging or running until it rests
chat.becameWinded: Too long without rest — the party is now winded!
chat.restedRecovered: The party has rested and is no longer winded.
chat.lightGuttering: {bearer}'s {light} is guttering — one turn of light remains!
chat.dayPassed: A full day of delve time has passed — consume rations and check spell recovery.
chat.encounterDetail: Maximum encounter distance {distance}'. Occurs at minute {minute} of the turn. Roll on the dungeon's encounter table and run the encounter (RR p. 280).
chat.saveMagical: Against a magical effect: each character's bonus vs magic and WIS modifier apply.
chat.saveMundane: Against a mundane effect: no bonus vs magic, no WIS modifier.
chat.fogLost: With no one mapping, the party's map of {scene} fades — the fog of war closes back in. Assign a Mapper who can work, with a light reaching them, to keep explored areas revealed.
chat.fogRestored: The mapper takes up the quill — explored areas of {scene} stay revealed on the map.
chat.detached: {name} moves out ahead of the party.
chat.combatDeployed: The formation breaks for battle — {n} member(s) deployed to the combat tracker.
chat.combatReformed: Combat over ({rounds} round(s)) — the party reforms into formation.
chat.combatFallen: Down and gathered up with the party: {names}. Assign Carriers to bring them along, or leave them behind where they fell — they keep their share of the experience either way.
chat.combatNoCombatants: No deployable members (all non-combatants or without tokens) — party token left in the tracker.
chat.combatTwinToken: This is not the party's own token, so nothing was deployed. Add the party's own token to the combat, or delete this copy.
chat.combatAlreadyFighting: Already fighting in {encounter} — the party token was taken back out of the tracker. End that encounter, or take the party's fighters out of it, to deploy again.
chat.bigMove: That drag consumed {turns} turn(s). If that was repositioning rather than exploration, use the undo-turn button or pause tracking.
chat.encounterNow: The wandering monsters arrive at minute {minute} of the turn — interrupt the party's movement here and run the encounter.
chat.signature: Party signature: {light}, {noise} — applies to surprise and earshot

warnings.inCombat: Members are deployed for combat — the party reforms automatically when the combat ends.
warnings.noMapper: No mapper assigned — without a map the party risks getting lost (assign the Mapper role).
warnings.mapperNoLight: No light reaches {names}: the module draws no map for this party and the scene's measurements read "?" (RR ch. 6, Marching and Mapping).
warnings.mapperDown: {names} cannot work the kit: the module draws no map for this party and the scene's measurements read "?" (RR ch. 6, Marching and Mapping).
warnings.mapperNoProficiency: No mapper who can work has the Mapping proficiency: the module warps the saved map and reads the scene's measurements vague (RR ch. 6, Marching and Mapping).
warnings.noLight: No lit light source — the party cannot see (unless members have shadowy senses or lightless vision).
warnings.winded: Winded: the party cannot charge or run until it rests (RR p. 271).
warnings.restDue: The party is due a rest — it must rest now or become winded (RR p. 271).
warnings.roleNoKit: {name} holds the {role} role without the kit it needs: {items}.
warnings.downNoCarrier: DOWN with no Carriers: {names} — the party cannot move (assign the Carrier role to bring them along, or leave them behind to march on; they keep their share either way).
warnings.carrying: Carrying {names}: {stone} stone total, split among {carriers} Carrier(s) ({share} st each) — carrier pace is recomputed with the load.
warnings.darkBlinded: Darkness: {blinded} cannot see and move as the blinded do. Seeing in the dark: {sighted}.
warnings.darkSighted: Darkness: the whole party operates on dark senses ({sighted}). No mapping or reading without bright light.

marching.saveHint: Remember this marching order — who stands where, what each of them is doing, and how many march abreast — under a name you can put the party back into later.
marching.loadHint: Put the party back into a saved marching order, or delete one you no longer use.
marching.nameHint: Saving under a name already in use replaces it.
marching.pickHint: Forming up gathers anyone standing on the map back inside the party token. Members the order does not name keep their place at the back; roles whose gear a character no longer holds are left off.
marching.none: No marching orders saved yet — arrange the party, then use Save order.
marching.notInCombat: The party cannot form up during a combat: the fight decides who is on the field. End the combat first.
marching.recalled: {count} gathered back into the party token.
marching.appended: {count} not named by the order kept their place at the back.
marching.absent: {count} named by the order are no longer in the party; the line closed up.
marching.noGear: Roles not restored for want of the gear they need: {names}.

hud.addToParty: Add to party (adds all controlled tokens; creates a formation if the scene has none)
hud.bringIn: Bring into the party (brings every controlled token of yours)
hud.formUp: Form up (put the party back into a saved marching order)

warn.noFormationYet: No formation exists yet — right-click a token and use "Add to party", or create a Party Formation actor.
warn.detachFailed: Nothing moved — the party has no token on the canvas to step out from.
warn.duplicatePartyToken: This formation already has a party token on the canvas — delete it first to re-place the party.
warn.summonCopy: {name} is the source copy of summoned creatures and cannot join a party; only a summoning cast's creatures do.
warn.summonerAbsent: {name} joins only the party its summoner marches in.
warn.summonInCombat: {name} cannot join {party} while a fight holds the party.
warn.frontageInvalid: Frontage is a whole number of ranks, one or more.
warn.frontageMax: This scene is only {max} squares wide — the party marches {max} abreast at most.
warn.forcedMarchBarred: The forced march is refused; the day stays as it was. Barred for: {names}.
warn.overburdened: Party exploration speed is 0 — someone is overburdened!
warn.spellNeedsName: Pick a spell or enter a name to track.
warn.spellNeedsTurns: Enter a duration in turns (the spell's duration couldn't be parsed).
warn.noRoleHands: {name} has no hands free for the {role} role: it takes {n}. Sheathe or stow something first.
warn.noRoleHandsHeld: {name} has no hands free for the {role} role: it takes {n} ({held}). Sheathe or stow something first.
warn.noFreeHand: {bearer} has no free hand to hold a light — sheathe or stow something to carry it properly.

notice.stowed: {name} puts away {items} to free a hand.

calendarSeasons.name: Calendar seasons
calendarSeasons.hint: Generator seasons in your calendar's season order, comma-separated (spring, summer, fall, winter). Blank matches the calendar's seasons by name.

transientIncidentTurns.name: Incident markers last (turns)
transientIncidentTurns.hint: When a city street produces an incident, a Judge-only marker is dropped where the party stood and removed after this many city turns on the world clock. 0 drops no marker.

partyTokenImage.name: Party token image
partyTokenImage.hint: Image used for the party token and party actor.

playersMoveParty.name: All players can move the party token
playersMoveParty.hint: Coarse override: grants every player owner rights on party actors. Normally unnecessary — players who own a member of a formation automatically get vision through, and control of, its party token.

partyTokenShape.name: Party token on the map
partyTokenShape.hint: The shape a party takes until its own sheet chooses one. Marching order: the party token is one square at the head, with the column drawn behind it along the ground it walked. Fixed size: the token keeps the size the Judge gives it, and nothing is drawn.

publicTurnCards.name: Public turn summaries
publicTurnCards.hint: Post the per-turn summary card publicly. Wandering-monster throws are always GM-whispered. Disable to whisper everything to the GM.

lightItemEnforcement.name: Light-source equipment
lightItemEnforcement.hint: Whether lighting a torch/candle/lantern requires the bearer to carry it (a lantern needs the lantern plus a flask of oil). When enforced, the fuel is consumed (the torch/candle, or a lantern's oil).

encounterEvery.name: Wandering monster throw frequency (turns)
encounterEvery.hint: Dungeon turns between automatic encounter throws. Blank uses the imported figure (JJ p. 36); 0 turns automatic throws off.

encounterTarget.name: Wandering monster target value
encounterTarget.hint: The encounter throw that meets a wandering monster, or better. Blank uses the imported figure (JJ p. 36).

restRequired.name: Require rests in the delve
restRequired.hint: Count dungeon turns toward a rest, warn when one is due and wind the party once it is overdue (RR p. 271). Turn off to drop all three; the clock and the wandering-monster throw keep running.

manageFog.name: Tie fog of war to the mapper
manageFog.hint: Fog exploration on a scene is fully disabled — neither shown nor recorded — unless a formation there has a member with the Mapper role. Current vision still shows. The scene's original fog mode is restored when the formation leaves or disbands. Scenes whose fog was already off are left alone.

mapperNeedsLight.name: Mapper requires a lit light source
mapperNeedsLight.hint: A Judge's automation switch. On: the module draws a map only while a light reaches the mapper's place (the day outside counts as light), and reads the scene's measurements "?" while none does. Off: it assumes light and reads none (RR ch. 6, Marching and Mapping).

syncTokenLight.name: Party token emits light
syncTokenLight.hint: Every lit, open light a member carries shines on the map from that member's place in the marching order, so players can see where they are even without a mapper (RR p. 265).

fuzzMeasurement.name: Fuzz player measurements without a proficient mapper
fuzzMeasurement.hint: On scenes where the party maps with no proficient mapper, players' ruler and drag distances show a hidden consistent error (~×0.8–1.25, rounded to the grid); while no party there is mapping at all they show "?". GMs always see true values. Players can still count grid squares — this is a deterrent, not a lock.

travelLogCap.name: Travel log length
travelLogCap.hint: How many finished days a formation's travel log keeps. Trimming eats the oldest days; it bounds the record's size, never the journey.

travelEncounters.name: Journey encounter throws
travelEncounters.hint: On by default: each cadence unit the march crosses and each finished day roll their owed encounter throws and whisper the chain to the Judge. Off, the party sheet's Encounter throw tool is the only trigger.

straggling.name: Crowded streets slow large parties
straggling.hint: A large party is slowed while commuting through a settlement, in tiers. The book marks this optional; the thresholds and the reduction come from your imported book.

provisionSharing.name: How a short day is shared
provisionSharing.hint: When the packs cannot feed the whole marching order, either everybody takes the same reduced ration, or as many as can be fed properly are and the rest go without. The book prices what going short does to a body, not who a captain chooses to feed.

weather.autoHint: When the calendar day changes the sky is rolled from the imported tables.
weather.frontsHint: Apply weather fronts to each day's throws (JJ ch. 2, Weather Fronts).
weather.generateHint: Three throws — temperature, precipitation, wind — under this hex's climate and the season.

enc.title: Wilderness encounter throw
enc.speaker: The Wilds
enc.throwHint: Roll the encounter chain for this hex and whisper the Judge the result.
enc.noRow: No printed row for this terrain — take the distance from the page.
enc.pickTerrain: No encounter terrain for this ground — pick one under Country on the Wilderness tab for the terrain-keyed steps.
enc.downgraded: {kind} stood down — the party is resting or retracing its own route.
enc.resolveBook: Resolve the entry from your book.
enc.visibleLine: The party can be seen from up to {feet}' in daylight ({size} heads).
enc.partyBlind: The party does not see them.
enc.monstersBlind: They do not see the party.
enc.handoff: Detection and surprise resolve on the system's Surprise Matrix when combat starts; reactions with the influence tools.
enc.zoneRowBlank: A blank row — the Judge decides what it holds.
enc.zoneTableGone: The table zone {zone} names cannot be found — draw this step by hand.

draw.exhausted: Roll limit reached — resolve the rest from your book.

day.trapsHint: Traps set or checked today; the day owes an encounter throw per batch.
day.noSleepHint: The order does not take its rest; End day counts it.

camp.waterHint: A river or lake beside the camp: water is taken without a throw.
camp.waterAuto: Water is already at hand here.
camp.sleepInArmourHint: Each sleeper throws against their encumbrance for a restful night.

travel.slotHint: One ancillary hour of the day.
travel.endDayHint: Log the day as shown, reset the board, and advance the world clock a day (when the module drives it).

dayEnd.title: The day's march is walked
dayEnd.body: {miles} mi walked in {hours} of the {budget} hours this day carries. Call the day done, or push on?
dayEnd.bodyUnpriced: {miles} mi walked in {hours} hours. Call the day done, or push on?

forcedBar.title: Forced march barred
forcedBar.body: A forced march is barred for: {names}. Set it anyway?
forcedBar.cancel: Leave the day as it is
forcedBar.note: The Judge set a forced march that was barred for: {names}.

travel.campDay: In camp — only hours given to travel walk.
travel.enterHexHint: The party crosses into the named hex; the day counts it.
travel.lostHint: GM only — the party does not know.
travel.windingHint: Following a winding road is longer than crossing straight. The road is usually still worth it — this is what it costs you in distance, so the trade is visible rather than hidden inside the miles.

movement.aloftHint: How much of the travelling day was spent in the air.
movement.dayHint: How long the travelling day was, in hours. Leave at zero for a day spent entirely aloft.
movement.loadHint: What the flier is carrying, which sets its speed band.
movement.replaced: {factor} is replaced by the flier's own.

travel.lostNote: Judge's note on the lost party

audit.title: Skill Audit
audit.openHint: Skill audit: see exactly how each party roll resolves per member, and flag custom skill items
audit.hint: How each party roll resolves for every member — the item or Adventuring target used, auto-scaled level, and bonuses. Rolls always use these live values.
audit.itemsHint: Flag ANY ability item to participate in a party roll (Used for). Unflagged items match by name and use their sheet target.
audit.sheetTargetTip: The target stored on the item's sheet.
audit.throwBonusHint: Flat adjustment to this item's party-roll throw: +2 makes the target 2 lower. Leave 0 for none.
audit.tableHint: A borrowed throw reads these rows at the level its own ability names. The rows are read from your own books at import — import skills to populate this.
audit.tabNotSkill: Not flagged as a party-roll skill. Set "Used for" to make this item participate in a party roll.
audit.isSkillHint: Mark this proficiency as a skill for party rolls. Turns on the Skill tab showing its live resolved target.
audit.rosterHint: Every distinct ability in the party, once. Automation matches by capability, explicit binding, or name — the union of all three. Click a ruling to force it off or on; the reset returns everything to automatic. Rulings are world-wide and keyed to the ability, so one decision covers every copy.
audit.resetHint: Clear every GM ruling and let automation decide again.
audit.resetConfirm: Clear all ability rulings and return every ability to automatic detection?
audit.overridden: Set by the GM — not automatic.
audit.toggleHint: Click to cycle: automatic → forced off → forced on → automatic.
audit.rollHint: Roll this ability for every party member who holds it: the party check's throw when one takes it, else the ability's own default throw. One card goes to the Judges; nothing else is advanced.
audit.rollNote: Skill audit roll: each holder rolled once.
audit.rollCannot: No roll, cannot attempt the party check: {names}.
audit.rollLacking: No roll, does not have it: {names}.
audit.rollNoThrow: No roll, the ability offers no throw: {names}.
audit.rollFailed: No roll, the throw could not be rolled: {names}.

route.binding: Bound explicitly on the item's Skill tab.
route.name: Matched by NAME only — this breaks if the item is renamed, and is the likeliest false positive. Bind it on the item's Skill tab to make it durable.

trapUuid.label: Trap
trapUuid.hint: The trap this region holds. Drag a Trap item here or paste its UUID. A region naming no trap resolves nothing.

state.label: State
state.hint: Armed until the party finds it. Found, disarmed and discharged traps are left alone when the party walks through.

repeatLock.label: Failed hasty attempts
repeatLock.hint: Who has already failed a hasty Trapbreaking attempt here, and at what level. Cleared by re-arming.

known.label: The party knows it is here
known.hint: Ticked, the party can see this trap and may work on it. Kept apart from the state: an armed trap can be known.

hint.kind: What this hazard adds to a place it is dropped on. Left at “—” it adds nothing.

HAZARD.noFigures: No figures here: length, gap and depth belong to each place this hazard is on, so one hazard can be two sizes in two places.

HAZARD_ENTRY.title: The party reaches
HAZARD_ENTRY.note: Begin opens that crossing with these figures and every condition of the places the party stands in.
HAZARD_ENTRY.beginTip: Open a crossing of this kind with this row’s figures and the conditions of the places the party stands in now.

confirm.title: Begin a crossing
confirm.body: A crossing is open ({open}). End it and begin {next}?

warn.mode: A journey or a settlement opens no crossing, so nothing was begun.
warn.left: The party no longer stands in {place}, so nothing was begun.
warn.gone: That obstacle is no longer on {place}, so nothing was begun.
warn.changed: The open crossing changed while you decided, so nothing was begun. Press Begin again.

traps.title: Trap
traps.toolLine: Trap the selected walls — with nothing selected, draw trap lines instead
traps.toolRegion: Enclose the selected walls as a trap area
traps.selectWalls: Select the walls to lay a trap along first.
traps.selectLoop: Select the walls enclosing the area — at least three.
traps.notClosed: Those walls do not close a shape. Join their ends and try again.
traps.laid: Trap laid on {added} wall(s). {skipped} already carried one.
traps.regionMade: Trap area created from the selected walls. Lifted the trap off {lifted} wall(s).
traps.foundNote: Found before anyone touched it. Describe the trigger and let them change what they were doing.
traps.crossedNote: The party crossed it and nothing happened. It is still armed.
traps.hurriedNote: At combat speed: no pole, and no hasty searching.
traps.sprungByPole: The pole took it, a square ahead of the party.
traps.caughtNobody: It fired into empty corridor and caught nobody.
traps.damageIsReported: Damage is reported, not applied — halve it for a made save, or set it aside, as the trap says.
traps.chooseHint: {name} has the trap beaten. Leave it disarmed, or set it off now?

disarm.disarmed: {name} disarms it. It can be re-armed.
disarm.botched: {name} sets it off — badly, and while standing over it.

refuse.noZone: The party is not standing at a trap.
refuse.noTrap: That trap has no Trap item assigned to it.
refuse.alreadyDischarged: That trap has already gone off.
refuse.cannotTry: {name} has no way to work on a trap.
refuse.alreadyFailedHasty: {name} has a failed hasty try recorded on this trap (RR p. 267).
refuse.notFound: Nobody has found that trap yet.

band.ownOver: Set on this trap, over the imported {band} ({page})

strip.label: Trap levels
strip.summary: Level {level} of {max} on screen; {filled} of {max} levels filled.
strip.summaryTip: Counted from this trap's rows: a level is filled when its text, damage, attack throw or pit depth is set.

resolution.none: Nothing rolled — the Judge narrates it

field.tierText: What the book says at this level

hint.level: 1st to 6th (JJ ch. 8, Trap Level). Chooses which row is edited below and which one fires when the trap goes off.
hint.trigger: How it is set off, in your own words: a tripwire, a pressure plate, a rune.
hint.triggerOn: Springs the trap on a secret die at or under this figure (RR ch. 6, Traps and Trapbreaking). Leave it blank to read the imported figure; 0 never springs.
hint.crude: Ticked, the trap takes the crude-trap adjustments to finding, removing and its effect.
hint.attackThrow: From your own book, for a fighter of this trap's level. Rolled against the victim's AC.
hint.damageFormula: What it deals, as dice. Leave blank for a pit and the depth below supplies it.
hint.pitDepthFeet: In feet. The fall's own damage is derived from it.
hint.spiked: Spikes at the bottom add their own damage to the fall.
hint.radiusFeet: In feet, from where it went off. Ranks within this distance are caught; a rank's depth is the column's, set in Scene config → Grid where the scene has no imported rank interval.
hint.rider: Prone, restrained, stuck, burning, a Mortal Wounds roll — printed on the card for you to apply.
hint.onSuccess: What a victim who makes the throw actually avoids.
hint.levelStrip: Filled levels are marked. A trap imported from the book states all six; one you wrote states the ones you filled in.
hint.tierText: The printed sentence for this level, kept whole. The fields below hold whatever could be read out of it.

traps.dropNoWall: Drop a trap onto a wall to assign it, or inside a region to add it to that region's place. There is neither here.
traps.wallTrapNone: None. Drag a Trap item here.
traps.wallTrapHint: Drag a Trap item onto this row to lay it on this wall. A trap blocks nothing on its own; it stops the party when it is found or springs.
traps.drew: Drew a trap line. Drag its ends into place.
traps.presetArmed: Trap line armed. Drag out the walls you want trapped; pick another wall type to stop.
traps.presetUnavailable: This Foundry build has no wall presets. Draw the wall, select it, and press this again.
traps.markerRebuilt: Spent trap rebuilt — armed again, and a fresh secret.
traps.markerRevealed: The party can see that trap now.
traps.markerHiddenNow: That trap is hidden from the party again.
traps.regionReused: That outline already had a trap area; reused it. Lifted the trap off {lifted} wall(s).

onSuccess.full: Nothing; the rider is the point

traps.sweepNote: {count} hidden trap(s) noticed in passing, off the line of march. The party has not walked into anything.
traps.breakHint: Work on a trap the party has found — choose who, which one, and how.
traps.breakNoActor: No character here is yours to act with.
traps.breakNothing: No trap the party has found is within reach. Search, or move up to one.
traps.breakJudgeHint: Judge only: unfound traps are listed so they can be marked found.
traps.breakListed: Only traps the party has found are listed.
traps.breakTouchingOnly: Only a trap the party touches is listed.
traps.stateFailedHasty: {name} failed a hasty try here at level {level}.
traps.stateNoFailedHasty: {name} has no failed hasty try here at level {level}.
traps.resetDone: The trap is rebuilt. Nobody knows it is there.

clock.day: The clock reads {time}: day, light from {dawn} to {dusk}.
clock.night: The clock reads {time}: after dark, light from {dawn} to {dusk}.
clock.unread: The world clock keeps no calendar to read an hour from, so it is treated as day. Choose By day or After dark instead.
clock.overridden: Set by hand; the clock reads {time}.

settlement.straggling: Crowded: the party is large enough to be slowed
settlement.noThrowRoute: The route is known; no throw is needed.
settlement.noThrowPace: A meandering pace reads the street signs; no throw is needed.
settlement.noThrowStationary: The party is staying put; a stay is thrown for by the day, not by the turn.
settlement.enterHint: Cross a settlement in blocks and turns instead of hexes and days.
settlement.cadence: The street answers every {turns} turn(s), on {target}+.

poi.travel: Go to a point of interest
poi.travelHint: Walk the party to a place on this map for the imported district-travel figure, instead of dragging the token block by block.
poi.travelTitle: Go to a point of interest
poi.noTargets: No place has a token on this map.

refused.noTarget: That place is no longer on the map.
refused.far: Those quarters do not touch. Move the token instead.
refused.outside: One end of the walk is outside every district. Draw the quarters first, or move the token.

poi.promoted: {name} is now a place on the map.

card.title: A turn in the streets
card.speaker: The city
card.marker: A marker was left where it happened.
card.strayed: Wrong turning — they end up {dice} blocks from where they meant to be.
card.met: Threw {rolled} on {die} against {target}+ — something finds them.
card.quiet: Threw {rolled} on {die} against {target}+ — the street lets them pass.
card.stillCatchingUp: {credited} day(s) thrown for so far; {left} still to catch up as the calendar advances.
card.interrupted: {count} day(s) did not pass quietly — day(s) {days}.

card.onRoad: Standing on {road} — {where}, read off the map.
card.onRoadUnnamed: Standing on {where}, read off the map.

settlement.trackBlocks: Timed by the map: a block here is {feet} {units}, so a turn is {turn} {units} walked.
settlement.trackWalk: This map has not said how big a block is, so the party is timed by its walking speed: a turn is {turn} {units}. Set the block size in Scene Configuration.
settlement.trackHoledUp: Staying put. Each day the calendar passes is thrown for.
settlement.trackNoMap: The party has no token on a map, so nothing is timing its turns yet.
settlement.conveyanceHint: How the party is carried. It sets no travel rate; a litter or wagon is marked private for the Judge.

note.incident: The street answers — see the city card.

settlement.notHoledUp: The party is out on the streets — pick a place to hole up first.

road.measuredStraight: Measured in a straight line — the move did not run along a drawn street.

settlement.cadenceInside: Inside {place}, the street answers every {turns} turn(s), on {target}+.
settlement.wantedHint: Somebody in this settlement is looking for this party: a district's hunted table answers instead of its ordinary one. A faction that wants the party sets this on its own in the quarters it controls; untick it and your word stands until the party enters another quarter.

district.noRegions: Select a region first — or draw one with the Regions tools.
district.regionMade: District region drawn from the selected walls.
district.regionReused: Those walls already had a district region — reused it.
district.noScene: No active scene to draw a district region on.
district.selectLoop: Select the walls that enclose the district — at least three.
district.notClosed: Those walls do not close a shape. Join their ends and try again.
district.refused: The district region could not be created.
district.markFailed: None of the selected regions could be marked as a district.
district.markPartial: Marked {count} of {total} region(s) as a district; the rest could not be changed.
district.notRegistered: The district region type is not registered on this server yet — shut the world down and relaunch it, then mark the region again.
district.toolError: That district tool could not finish; see the console for what stopped it.

settlement.streetDie: the die the street's encounter is thrown on
settlement.cadenceSplit: Not the street's rhythm: every {turns} turn(s) from {turnsFrom}, on {target}+ from {targetFrom}.
settlement.strayHint: If the throw fails, they end up {dice} blocks off course.

lists.wanted: Incidents here: {table}, the quarter's table while the party is hunted.
lists.district: Incidents here: {table}, the quarter's own table. It replaces the city table, so the quarter's special table is never reached.
lists.band: A total of {from} to {to} is handed to {table}.
lists.bandDark: A total of {from} to {to} is handed to {table}, {shift} after dark.
lists.bandNone: A total of {from} to {to} has no special table to go to here.
lists.world: Incidents here: the world's own city table. This map names none of its own.
lists.missing: {list} named here no longer exists, so the next table answers. Name it again, or run the importer's Maps step to repair the map.
lists.specialMissing: The quarter's special table cannot be read, so the city table's own row stands. Name it again, or run the importer's Maps step to repair the map.

discovered.title: You are not where you thought
discovered.body: Landmarks that should have been here are not, and ones that should not, are. The ground you have been marking down these past days was never yours to map.
discovered.drift: {days} day(s) astray; {hexes} hex(es) have gone back under the fog.
discovered.hint: You can set off again in the direction you meant. Where you strayed, you do not know — unless you double back the way you came.

lost.askBody: The throw failed and the party does not know it. Choose the face they took — from the landmarks and the lie of the land — or let the dice decide.
lost.askHint: They will keep believing they went the way they meant to, and the map will fill in accordingly.
lost.needHex: The party has no hex recorded yet, so there is nowhere to stray from.
lost.noNeighbour: That hex has no neighbour on this grid.
lost.astraySince: Astray for {days} day(s); {hexes} hex(es) of map they did not earn.
lost.beginHint: Open an episode: pick the face they actually took, and the table's map begins filling in the wrong place.
lost.discoverHint: Marks the party aware that it is lost. Its position is not revealed, and the hexes it mapped while astray are cleared from the fog.
lost.reanchorHint: The only ending that gives anything back: the country they really crossed is put onto the map, in its right place.
lost.awareSince: They know they are lost; {days} day(s) since they strayed.
lost.leftover: A true-position marker from an earlier episode is still on the map.
lost.endHint: Close the episode and credit nothing: the ground they drew wrongly closes over, the party token stays where it stands, and the true-position marker is removed.
lost.leftoverMoveHint: Move the party token onto the leftover marker, then remove the marker.
lost.leftoverClearHint: Delete the leftover marker. The party token stays where it is.
lost.viewScene: Open the scene the party stands on first: a lost episode's map is drawn there.
lost.reanchorBody: The ground they really crossed is put onto the map in its right place, and the true-position marker is removed.
lost.reanchorMove: Move the party token onto its true position

nav.title: Finding the way
nav.speaker: The Judge's compass
nav.one: Someone in the order knows the country.
nav.both: Two ways of knowing the country, and they compound.
nav.botched: The throw failed automatically (RR ch. 6, Navigation).
nav.kept: They are where they think they are.
nav.lost: They have strayed, and do not know it.
nav.judgeChooses: Begin it once you are there: the shadow starts on the party's hex, and you shift the truth from the Judge tab as they walk on.
nav.noHex: The lost episode could not be opened: the party stands on no hex of a map yet. Walk the party token onto a hex, then begin it.
nav.aware: They already know they are lost. The episode stays as it is.
nav.astrayKept: Thrown true while they are astray. The episode stays open.
nav.astrayLost: Thrown false while they are astray. The episode stays open.
nav.opened: The lost episode is open: the shadow stands on the party's hex. Shift the truth from the Judge tab as they walk on.
nav.notOpened: The lost episode could not be opened from here: view the party's scene, then begin it from this card.

camp.thirsty: the heat is drinking it faster
camp.thirstyHint: Today's weather raises the water need per person, so the days of water shown are fewer (RR 277–279).
camp.exposureHoursHint: Hours the order stood unprotected today. A member carrying weather clothing counts as sheltered (RR 277–279).

forageRun.title: What the country gave
forageRun.speaker: The day's work
forageRun.automatic: {kind}: taken freely here, no throw needed.
forageRun.workHint: Roll the day's foraging and hunting for the whole order, and put what is found into their packs.
forageRun.noHours: No hours were set aside for foraging or hunting today.
forageRun.worked: Every hunting and foraging hour is already spent today.

searchRun.title: An hour of looking
searchRun.speaker: The search
searchRun.looking: Looking for {quarry}: {target}+, modifier {modifier}, {throws} attempt(s) this hour.
searchRun.nothingHere: Threw {total} — good enough, but there is nothing here to find.
searchRun.silence: The party learns nothing, and cannot tell an empty hex from a poor search.
searchRun.watched: The hour owes its encounter throw — looking around gets you noticed.
searchRun.searchHint: Spend one of the day's set-aside hours looking. It owes an encounter throw whatever it finds.
searchRun.presentHint: The stock's answer, or the Judge's own.

hexStock.title: This hex
hexStock.noScene: No map hex to keep a stock under. Set the journey's hex, or put the party on a map.
hexStock.astray: The party is astray; this is where it really stands.
hexStock.noSurveyor: Nobody in the order holds Land Surveying.
hexStock.alreadyPlaced: This point is already a place.
hexStock.restockConfirm: {hex} is already stocked. Replace its stock, finds and survey?
hexStock.clearConfirm: Clear the stock of {hex}? Its points, finds and survey are removed.

dialog.title: Stock the hex
dialog.substituteHint: Roll each lair on the substitution table (JJ 69).
dialog.countHint: Overrides the roll when set (JJ 69). Required when the terrain has no imported row.
dialog.needsCount: This terrain has no count to roll. Type one.

survey.speaker: The surveyor
survey.title: Land Surveying
survey.askJudge: Supply a count to tell the party.
survey.public: The surveyor reckons {count} point(s) of interest here.

bar.journeyTitle: Hours walked today, of the day's travel budget
bar.restTitle: Turns since the party last rested, of the rest interval

presses.rationOwned: press to ration the members you own

key.title: Key
key.sub: The rails are the same on every tab; only the figures read differently.
key.sheet: Sheet tools · right of the reading
key.foot: A mode's own actions sit at the head of its tab.

head.journeySub: The journey's own actions; the rails hold what every mode shares.

head.citySub: The city's own actions; the rails hold what every mode shares.
head.orderSub: Who walks where, and what each of them does.
head.sightingsSub: The road so far, day by day.
head.judgeSub: Only the Judge's seat renders this tab.
head.delveTip: Turn {turns}: the turns this party's clock has spent, and {elapsed} of game time (RR p. 263)
head.cityTip: Turn {turns}: the turns this party's clock has spent in the city (RR p. 263)
head.journeyTip: Day {day}: the days this journey has logged with End day (RR ch. 6, Wilderness Expeditions)
head.asks: Turn and Round ask the Judge.

judge.offJourney: An episode opens on a journey; there is none in this mode.

sightings.empty: No day has been logged yet.
sightings.offJourney: The log is kept on a journey.

checks.title: Party checks
checks.prompt: Which check does the party make?

chip.overrideHint: The Judge's word stands over the map, which reads {map}.
chip.declared: Declared, with nothing on the map under it

country.paintHint: Arms the country brush on this card's layer and opens its palette. Nothing is painted until you click the map.

plate.ariaNoHex: The hex the party stands in, drawn

where.same: The truth and the belief are the same hex.
where.noShadow: No shadow stands for this party on the episode's scene.

shown.believedHint: Players see the hex the party token stands in, drawn, with its country.
shown.unknownHint: Players see a blank plate, no hex label and no country.

navigation.owed: Owed at the day's first step off the road.
navigation.throwNowHint: Makes the navigation throw now, whispered to the Judge. It counts as the day's throw.
navigation.nothingOwed: Nothing to throw: the party is following a road or a route.

tip.speedHurried: Hurried: combat speed {combat}' a round, {feet}' a turn

REGION_PLACE.label: Place
REGION_PLACE.dropHidden: A trap you drop is hidden, as every trap is, and is not counted here.
REGION_PLACE.create: Make a place for this region
REGION_PLACE.hint: The place that holds this region's traps, obstacles and conditions. The plus button makes one, filed under the scene's own place.
REGION_PLACE.holdsNone: Holds no traps, obstacles or conditions yet.
REGION_PLACE.drop: Drop a trap, obstacle or condition here. With no place yet, one is made.
REGION_PLACE.dropOwned: Drop a trap, obstacle or condition here.

refused.notItem: Only an item can be dropped here.
refused.blankHazard: That hazard has no kind set. Set its kind on its sheet, then drop it again.
refused.notAccepted: Only a trap, an obstacle or a condition can be dropped here.
refused.noPlace: No place could be made for this region.
refused.noRegion: Drop it inside a region that has no zone or terrain of its own, or on a place, to add it there.

place.label: The quarter's place
place.hint: The location actor this quarter IS — its market, its notes, what is kept there. Pick one, or make one named after the region.
place.create: Make a place for this quarter

tableUuid.label: District encounter table
tableUuid.hint: RollTable drawn from (privately) when the streets throw for the party anywhere in this district. Drag a RollTable here or paste its UUID.

wantedTableUuid.label: Table when they are hunted
wantedTableUuid.hint: Drawn from instead, while the party's settlement board is marked hunted here. Empty = use the table above.

specialTableUuid.label: Special encounters table
specialTableUuid.hint: Read when the city table named in this scene's configuration rolls inside its district band: thrown on its own formula, the figure below added after dark. Leave the district encounter table empty for this to be reached.

specialAfterDark.label: Special table: added after dark
specialAfterDark.hint: Added to the special table's own throw once the board says after dark, which is how its rows past the die are reached. Blank = nothing added. The importer's Maps step fills a blank one from the table's own rows.

encounterEveryDay.label: Throw frequency by day (turns)
encounterEveryDay.hint: Make an encounter throw every N city turns in this district while it is light. 0 = inherit the layer outside this district.

encounterEveryNight.label: Throw frequency after dark (turns)
encounterEveryNight.hint: As above, once the board says after dark. 0 = inherit.

encounterTargetDay.label: Target value by day (JJ ch. 7)
encounterTargetDay.hint: Encounter occurs on this value or higher in this district while it is light. 0 = inherit the layer outside this district.

encounterTargetNight.label: Target value after dark (JJ ch. 7)
encounterTargetNight.hint: As above, once the board says after dark. 0 = inherit.

reactionModifier.label: Reaction adjustment
reactionModifier.hint: Added to reaction and influence throws made in this district (JJ ch. 7). Negative where strangers are unwelcome; 0 for a quarter that is unremarkable.

reactionWhere.label: Where it applies
reactionWhere.hint: Which part of the district the adjustment is owed in.

ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.created: Posting created: {total} candidate(s) this month. Week-1 search fee: {fee} gp.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.commissionedHint: Run this search as a commission, renewed while it stands. Its rarity eases {steps} step(s) toward common (JJ ch. 3, "Commissioning the Hire of a Henchman").
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.commissioned: Commissioned search: it renews as a commission (JJ ch. 3, "Commissioning the Hire of a Henchman").
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.commissionedHintCi: JJ ch. 3, "Commissioning the Hire of a Henchman"
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.domainRulerHint: Judges a leveled search by a domain ruler's cap instead of the employer-level ladder (RR 168).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.networkHint: Whether this search uses the employer's mercantile network here: its candidates and its weekly fee are read at the class the network makes the market (RR ch. 2, Mercantile Network).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.networkUsed: Searched with the employer's mercantile network.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.networkNotCounted: Not counted here for {name}: no earlier visit is on record.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.networkMissing: {power} has no value imported; re-import the class powers, or give it an Active Effect.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.presentedLevelHint: The level this posting shows candidates in place of the employer's own. The level cap reads it, and a henchman hired from the posting keeps it on their record for the loyalty roll to weigh against the true level (RR 168).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.liedLevel: GM only: employer presented as level
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.weekHint: Week of the current availability month. The month's pool arrives in shares across its weeks (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.poolHint: Availability rolled for each specification. Hover a row for the roll detail.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.toggleDetails: Toggle whether players see this posting's candidate details
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.none: No recruitment postings. A posting pays the weekly search fee (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.levelCapError: {employer} cannot hire level {level} henchmen (cap: level {cap}, RR 168).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.classLevelHint: Leave level blank to search by class alone. A named level replaces only that level's rolled henchmen, searched {steps} rarity step(s) higher per level above 1st (JJ ch. 3, "Rarity of Henchmen").
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.classLevelHintCite: Leave level blank to search by class alone (JJ ch. 3, "Rarity of Henchmen").
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.no-market: This place has no market to post a notice in.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.fee-refused: The search fee could not be paid here, so nothing was posted.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.feeRefused: {name}'s search in {location} has ended: this week's fee could not be paid.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.duplicate-sp: That specification has already been searched this month (JJ 118).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.duplicate-se: That hiring character already has an active search for this hireling type here — the market's pool is shared (RR 162).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.privateHint: Private specific search (JJ 118): paid and rolled separately for this recruiter.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.criteriaHint: Pick what you are paying to see: the general henchman market, a mercenary or specialist type — or a directed search that replaces rolled henchmen with what you seek.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.criteria-req: A post must name what you are looking for — a class, proficiency, troop or specialist type.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.level-requir: A leveled search must name the level — it sets the price.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.not-yours: You can only post on behalf of a character you own.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.submitted: Posting submitted — the GM client rolls the search.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.advertVeteranHint: Advertised a full market month: it renews as a commissioned search while the post stays up (JJ ch. 3, "Commissioning the Hire of a Henchman").
ACKS-HENCHMEN.market.hint: This location's hireling availability (RR 162): each hireling type rolled at the location's market class, one pool for every recruiter. A posting is a paid search of it.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.market.empty: Nothing rolled this month. Create a posting to canvass the market.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.demographicsHint: Weighted culture mix used to generate candidate names, ages, and appearances (RR 495-503). Empty = uniform random.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixDropHint: Drop a RollTable of cultures here to set this town's culture mix (result text = culture, weight = share).
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixExport: Export the culture mix as a RollTable (prefilled) — tweak it, then drop it back here.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixTableHint: Culture mix for a settlement. Tweak entries/weights, then drop this table onto the location sheet's demographics block to apply.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixExported: Culture mix exported as "{name}" — tweak and drop it back on the sheet.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.mixNoCultures: "{name}" has no recognizable culture entries — result text must be a culture name or id.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.location.demographicsEmpty: No demographics set — candidates draw from all cultures evenly.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.repair.swept: Repaired dangling hireling references on {count} actor(s): deleted hirelings were still listed on their employers.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.repair.check.label: Hireling lists naming actors that are gone
ACKS-HENCHMEN.repair.check.hint: An employer's hireling list, a monster hireling list or a hireling's employer naming an actor that has been deleted, or a hireling listed twice. Fixing removes the dead entries. A hireling whose employer is gone stays a hireling, with no employer.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.repair.check.wageType.hint: A mercenary group hired from the market's combined composite and longbow entry before wage types were stored, so payroll finds no wage for it. Fixing stores the type from the settlement the group was hired at, as it is today. A group whose settlement is gone is listed and left alone.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.repair.check.wageType.noSe: the settlement it was hired at is gone
ACKS-HENCHMEN.setting.autoRepairReferenc: At world load, remove references to deleted hirelings from employers' rosters. With this off, a GM can run acksExtras.henchmen.repair.repairWorld() from the console instead.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.unknown-clas: That class is not in the location's rarity table.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.class-blocke: That class is never offered at this place.
ACKS-HENCHMEN.posting.error.past-legenda: Rarer than Legendary — not findable by this method (JJ 119).
